name: base-003-federation-cache-staleness-nondeterminism
description: NOT FIXED - base-game (non-Lost-Fleet) caching bug, out of this session's LF-focused triage scope, surfaced (not caused) by a Lost Fleet ship-federation claim move. A fresh sequential replay (new Engine(moves)) ends up offering NO Command.FormFederation at all at the point of the final line, while host-style incremental play (Engine.slowMotion, fromData-clone-and-replay-the-partial-line per move, matching what both real hosts do) correctly offers it. Root-caused via a full instrumented trace: the two engines' normalizedEngineState (all occupied hexes, resources, map, etc.) is BYTE-IDENTICAL once player.federationCache is excluded from comparison - the divergence is entirely inside federationCache itself. Player.availableFederations() (player.ts) has an early-return cache-hit path keyed only on `maxSatellites <= federationCache.availableSatellites`, with no check that the underlying occupied-hex set hasn't changed since the cache was warmed; on the replay path the cache ends up permanently stuck at an early, empty {federations: []} snapshot despite several later 'build m' moves that should have invalidated it via player.build()'s `if (!wasOccupied) { ...; this.federationCache = null }` branch. Root cause not fully isolated within this session's time budget (candidates include hex object-identity mismatches between the coordinate-resolved hex used by build() and the one already in data.occupied, or a call-frequency difference in when generateAvailableCommands()/availableFederations() gets invoked between sequential loadMoves() processing and per-part host-style replay). federationCache is base-game machinery (federations exist in vanilla Gaia Project) with no RULES_CLARIFICATIONS.md entry to cite, so per the owner's explicit instruction for this session (trust the base implementation, focus on Lost Fleet rules) this was investigated far enough to classify and document but not fixed. Flagged for a future base-game-focused session; this fixture is a fully reproducible minimal repro (shrunk from 58 to 35 lines via fuzz/shrink.ts).
